h1:
Nonthaburi Boat Noodles
8 Old-School Shops with Bold Broth
intro: Nonthaburi is real boat-noodle country: thick, dark broth, a warm hit of white pepper, tiny bowls meant to be ordered several at a time, eaten with crisp fried pork rinds. From long-running shops in the old town to riverside places near Pak Kret where you dangle your feet over the water, these are the spots locals actually go to — with areas and prices so you can plan your trip.
chips: 🐷 Crispy pork rinds with every bowl

blocks.html: Boat noodles weren't born in Nonthaburi exactly, but this stretch of the lower Chao Phraya — Nonthaburi and Ayutthaya — is where the dish grew up, sold straight from boats in the canals. These days everything has moved onto dry land, but the charm is all still there: small bowls, deep broth, bold and fully seasoned. Locals eat them from morning into the afternoon, and plenty of these shops have been open for decades. We've pulled together both easy-to-drive-to spots in town and riverside places where you'll want to leave time to sit and relax.

blocks.text: What makes Nonthaburi boat noodles good

blocks.html: The heart of boat noodles is the broth. The shops locals keep coming back to tend to simmer bones for hours, add blood to thicken the soup, then season with spices and pepper until it's deep and well rounded. The traditional small bowl is small on purpose — you order several so each one arrives with the broth still piping hot. Eat them with fish balls, slow-braised beef or fall-apart pork, then finish with crispy fried pork rinds dipped in the soup.

items: Thick, deep broth — the well-known shops simmer bones for hours and add fresh blood, which makes the soup rich and heavy with a deep flavour.
Traditional small bowls — around 15–20 THB a bowl, and ordering 4–6 bowls each is completely normal.
Full range of options — thin rice noodles, wide noodles or egg noodles, pork or beef, with fish balls and braised toppings.
Pork rinds on the side — almost every shop has crispy fried pork rinds, and dipping them in the broth works perfectly.

blocks.text: 8 boat noodle shops Nonthaburi locals go to

blocks.html: We've ordered these by how long they've been around, how bold the flavour is, and what locals say in their reviews. The prices listed are rough ranges based on what the shops post and recent reviews — they can shift depending on what toppings you order. We'd suggest checking each shop's weekly closing day before you set off, since several close mid-week.

items.name: Kuaytiao Ruea Nai Klae Bang Si Mueang
items.blurb: A long-running shop open for over 20 years in the Bang Si Mueang area, with rich, boldly seasoned old-school broth. The big draw is the long hours — open until 9pm, so you can have it for dinner, unlike most boat-noodle shops that shut by mid-afternoon.
items.meta: Bang Si Mueang, Mueang Nonthaburi · open 9:00am–9:00pm daily

items.name: Kuaytiao Ruea Hua Ruea Sai Ma
items.blurb: Tucked into a lane in Ban Sai Ma, central Nonthaburi, known for thick, heavy broth and a clear hit of white pepper. It's where people in the area meet up for a late-morning bowl, and it's an easy drive from town.
items.meta: Soi Ban Sai Ma, Mueang Nonthaburi · open 8:00am–4:00pm

items.name: Kuaytiao Ruea Boran Mae Daeng
items.blurb: On Soi Ngamwongwan 31 and easy to reach, with thick, full-flavoured broth and generously loaded bowls. Open late into the evening every day, so it suits anyone who wants boat noodles in the late afternoon or evening — order the fried pork rinds to go with it.

items.name: Kuaytiao Lung Tao by the Chao Phraya River
items.blurb: A riverside shop on Soi Nonthaburi 27/6 in the Tha Sai area, where you sit and catch the breeze right by the river. The broth is nicely balanced, prices are friendly, and there's fried oyster omelette and hoi tod to add on. Best in the morning through to the afternoon.
items.meta: Soi Nonthaburi 27/6, Tha Sai · open 8:00am–3:00pm (closed Sunday)

items.name: Kuaytiao Ruea Ayutthaya Phi Mee
items.blurb: Around the Ban Tha It–Ban Sai Ma area near Bang Rak Noi, Mueang Nonthaburi, done in Ayutthaya boat-noodle style. Known for crispy fried pork rinds and rich broth. It gets packed on weekends, so allow time to wait.
items.meta: Ban Tha It, Bang Rak Noi, Mueang Nonthaburi · open 9:00am–5:00pm (closed Monday)

items.name: Tiao Ruea Ko Baen Bang Krang
items.blurb: A garden shop by a pond in the Bang Krang area of Bang Kruai, where you sit under little salas surrounded by water and trees. There are herbal drinks to order too, and it suits coming as a family and settling in for a while.
items.meta: Samakkhi Rd, Bang Krang, Bang Kruai · open 9:00am–5:30pm (closed Tuesday)

items.name: Kuaytiao Ruea Hoi Kha Lung Ut
items.blurb: A riverside shop where you really do sit with your feet dangling over the canal, with an easygoing garden-house feel. The broth is on the milder side, not overly punchy, so it's good for bringing along anyone who doesn't eat much spice. Open morning to afternoon.

items.name: Phayao Kuaytiao Boran Tha It
items.blurb: An old-style shop in the Tha It area of Pak Kret, with traditional-recipe broth and easy starting prices. Open from late morning into the evening, with longer hours on weekends — handy for a stop on the way to Koh Kret.

blocks.title: How to order for the best bowl
blocks.html: The small bowls are meant to be ordered in numbers — start with 3–4 at a time so you get them while the broth is still piping hot, then order more. Don't skip the fried pork rinds for dipping in the soup, and if you like it bold, just ask the staff to add more chilli flakes and vinegar.

blocks.text: How to pick the right shop for you

items.name: You want bold, deep, traditional flavour
items.blurb: Go for Nai Klae in Bang Si Mueang or Hua Ruea in Sai Ma — thick, heavy broth with a clear hit of pepper.

items.name: You want to relax by the water
items.blurb: Lung Tao on the Chao Phraya or Hoi Kha Lung Ut — you get the river setting and a cool breeze.

items.name: Coming as a family, settling in
items.blurb: Tiao Ruea Ko Baen in its garden, with salas and herbal drinks — easy for kids to sit comfortably.

items.name: Stopping on the way to Koh Kret
items.blurb: Phayao Kuaytiao Boran in the Tha It area of Pak Kret is right on the same route.

items: Central Nonthaburi — Sai Ma, Bang Si Mueang and Ngamwongwan have the most shops. Take the Purple Line metro and grab a taxi or motorbike from there.
Pak Kret — Tha It and Bang Phlap have both old-style and garden shops, perfect to fold into a trip to Koh Kret.
Bang Kruai — Bang Krang has garden shops beside a pond, leafy and shaded; driving is easier here than public transport.
Avoid peak hours — the popular shops fill up from late morning (around 11am) into the afternoon, and even more so on weekends. Arrive before 11am and you'll find a seat far more easily.

faq.q: Which Nonthaburi boat noodle shop is old and good?
faq.a: The ones locals mention most are Nai Klae in Bang Si Mueang, open for over 20 years and serving until 9pm, plus Hua Ruea in Sai Ma and Mae Daeng on Ngamwongwan. All of them stand out for thick, rich, boldly seasoned old-school broth.

faq.q: How much do Nonthaburi boat noodles cost?
faq.a: Most traditional small-bowl shops run about 15–20 THB a bowl, and people usually order 4–6 bowls each. Some shops have large bowls starting around 40 THB. Fried pork rinds and add-ons are charged separately.

faq.q: Where can I eat boat noodles by the river in Nonthaburi?
faq.a: Try Lung Tao by the Chao Phraya River in the Tha Sai area, or Hoi Kha Lung Ut where you actually sit with your feet over the canal. Tiao Ruea Ko Baen in Bang Krang is a garden shop by a pond, good for settling in for a while.

faq.q: What time do Nonthaburi boat noodle shops open?
faq.a: Most open morning to afternoon, roughly 8–9am until 3 or 4pm. A few, like Nai Klae and Mae Daeng, stay open into the evening, but many have a weekly closing day mid-week, so it's worth checking before you go.

faq.q: What time should I go to avoid a long wait?
faq.a: The popular shops get busy from late morning into the afternoon, especially on weekends. Go before 11am and you'll find a seat more easily, with the broth still fresh.
